answer: Each epoch the network publishes a fresh cipher and every agent forges a seal over its task output: a keyed encryption under a key mixing its own secret with the epoch cipher, so only its owner opens it. Three random peers check each seal decrypts to a task actually run and compare plaintexts across the reef; two seals opening to one output expose a clone farm at once, both identities quarantined, rewards frozen three epochs. Copying one solution across 1,000 masks needs 1,000 keys and 1,000 runs, about 400 GPU-hours per epoch, while one honest agent forges its seal in milliseconds, free.
